statusLevels.documented: From manufacturer manuals and source research only. Not yet tried with Aether DV.
statusLevels.reported: Operators report it working (see field reports). Not yet verified by the project.
statusLevels.tested: Tested with Aether DV on this radio (hardware level), with captures.

general: Connect the radio's DV Data port (not its programming or CI-V port) and note the serial device; `serial-spike list` shows candidates without opening any.
Set the radio to DV mode and "DV Data TX" to Auto, so it keys up when data arrives.
Turn GPS TX (position beacons) off while using data: it shares the same slow-data channel.
Leave Fast Data off on shared frequencies. Fast Data stations cannot decode slow ones and vice versa.

On a repeater: tell Aether DV which repeater (call sign and module) and who should receive your data (this repeater only, or the linked reflector). Set the radio to match: UR = CQCQCQ, R1 = the repeater, and R2 blank for this repeater only. R2 = the gateway (the repeater's call with G) sends everything to every repeater linked to the reflector. Aether DV holds sending until the route matches.
Store a memory channel used only for data, with UR, R1 and R2 already set. Voice use then can't change the data route by accident.

radios.name: IC-9700
radios.summary: Base station, 2 m / 70 cm / 23 cm. USB port B carries DV data while port A stays CI-V, so Aether can also check the Fast Data setting.
radios.fastData: yes (firmware 1.50 or later improves the end-of-Fast-Data beep)
radios.connection: USB (B) for DV data, USB (A) for CI-V. 9600 baud. Use the port the programming software is not using.

steps.title: Radio menus
items: SET > Connectors > USB (B)/DATA Function > USB (B) Function = DV Data (USB A stays CI-V)
SET > Connectors > CI-V > CI-V Transceive = OFF (Aether DV polls what it needs; less load on the radio)
SET > DV/DD Set > DV Data TX = Auto
SET > DV/DD Set > DV Fast Data > Fast Data = OFF (slow data, for shared nets)
MENU > GPS > GPS TX Mode = OFF

steps.title: Aether DV
items: Start from examples/ic9700.toml: profile = "icom-ic9700", baud = 9600, mode = "slow".
Optional: add [port.civ] with the USB (A) device; the IC-9700's default CI-V address is A2h. Aether then warns at start-up if the radio's Fast Data setting doesn't match the port's mode.

steps.title: Using a repeater
items: Set the radio to the repeater's channel (duplex) as for voice.
For this repeater only: UR = CQCQCQ, R1 = repeater call and module (e.g. W4DOC  B), R2 blank. In DR mode this is "Local CQ".
For the linked reflector: R2 = the repeater's gateway (e.g. W4DOC  G), UR = CQCQCQ ("Gateway CQ" in DR mode). Only do this with the trustee's agreement.
Never leave a link or unlink command in UR (e.g. REF030CL or "       U") with R2 on the gateway: every data transmission would send it again. Aether DV blocks this when it can read UR.

Aether DV reads UR/R1/R2, duplex and the receive status over CI-V (USB A). It holds sending when the radio is set for another route, and waits while voice is on the channel. Documented in Icom's CI-V guide; not yet tested on a radio (HW-R1).

radios.name: ID-52 PLUS
radios.summary: Handheld, 2 m / 70 cm. USB-C carries either DV data or CI-V, not both; Bluetooth can carry the other.
radios.connection: USB-C with Serialport Function = DV Data. For CI-V at the same time, use the Bluetooth serial port (Serialport Function = CI-V there).

steps.title: Radio menus
items: [MENU] > SET > Function > USB Connect = Serialport
[MENU] > SET > Function > USB Serialport Function = DV Data
[MENU] > SET > DV Set > DV Data TX = Auto
DV Fast Data OFF (slow data)
GPS TX OFF

steps.title: Aether DV
items: Start from examples/id52plus.toml: profile = "icom-id52plus", mode = "slow".
CI-V (optional, over Bluetooth): the default address reported for the ID-52 is B4h, not confirmed for the PLUS; check MENU > SET > Function > CI-V and set civ.addr.

steps.title: Using a repeater
items: Set the radio to the repeater's channel (duplex) as for voice.
For this repeater only: UR = CQCQCQ, R1 = repeater call and module (e.g. W4DOC  B), R2 blank. In DR mode this is "Local CQ".
For the linked reflector: R2 = the repeater's gateway (e.g. W4DOC  G), UR = CQCQCQ ("Gateway CQ" in DR mode). Only do this with the trustee's agreement.
Never leave a link or unlink command in UR (e.g. REF030CL or "       U") with R2 on the gateway: every data transmission would send it again. Aether DV blocks this when it can read UR.

Over a CI-V connection (Bluetooth while USB carries data) Aether DV tries to read UR/R1/R2 and the receive status. Not yet confirmed on this model: if the radio refuses, Aether DV asks you to confirm the route instead.

radios.name: ID-51 PLUS / PLUS2
radios.summary: Handheld with a DATA jack. Install the 2019-11 firmware, which fixes data loss.

steps.title: Radio menus (as published for the ID-51 by W5AW)
items: MENU > GPS > GPS SET > GPS SELECT = OFF
MENU > GPS > GPS SET > GPS OUT (DATA jack) = OFF
MENU > FUNCTION > CI-V > CI-V (DATA jack) = OFF
MENU > FUNCTION > DATA SPEED = 9600

steps.title: Using a repeater
items: Set the radio to the repeater's channel (duplex) as for voice.
For this repeater only: UR = CQCQCQ, R1 = repeater call and module (e.g. W4DOC  B), R2 blank. In DR mode this is "Local CQ".
For the linked reflector: R2 = the repeater's gateway (e.g. W4DOC  G), UR = CQCQCQ ("Gateway CQ" in DR mode). Only do this with the trustee's agreement.
Never leave a link or unlink command in UR (e.g. REF030CL or "       U") with R2 on the gateway: every data transmission would send it again. Aether DV blocks this when it can read UR.

Aether DV can't read this radio's call signs or detect voice. It asks you to confirm the route each session and after 30 minutes without sending, and uses shorter transmissions with longer gaps. Pause sending during voice contacts and nets.
Firmware: use the November 2019 release or later, which fixes data loss.

radios.name: TM-D750
radios.summary: 2026 mobile. Whether its USB/Bluetooth data port carries D-STAR DV data the way D-RATS needs is not known yet; no software control of Fast Data is documented.
radios.connection: USB and Bluetooth. Its D-STAR "Reflector Terminal Mode" uses a different (MMDVM) protocol and does not transmit on RF.

steps.title: Status
items: Not yet set up with Aether DV. If you try it, send a report: menu path for DV data, baud rate, and whether chat and a small file worked.

steps.title: Using a repeater
items: Set the repeater in the radio's D-STAR settings as for voice (DR or the repeater list).
For this repeater only: UR = CQCQCQ, RPT1 = repeater call and module, RPT2 blank. For the linked reflector: RPT2 = the repeater's gateway (call with G), only with the trustee's agreement.
Never leave a link or unlink command in UR with RPT2 on the gateway.
No documented way to read the call signs or receive status: Aether DV asks you to confirm the route. Data on this radio is still unverified.

radios.name: TH-D75
radios.summary: Handheld. Reported to behave like the TH-D74 for D-RATS (receive reported; transmit unconfirmed).
radios.connection: USB-C (the serial control line DTR must be on); Bluetooth serial (Menu 984). Menu 614 must not be Off.

steps.title: Radio menus
items: Menu 614 not Off; check the manual for the DV data setting

steps.title: Using a repeater
items: Set the repeater in the radio's D-STAR settings as for voice (DR or the repeater list).
For this repeater only: UR = CQCQCQ, RPT1 = repeater call and module, RPT2 blank. For the linked reflector: RPT2 = the repeater's gateway (call with G), only with the trustee's agreement.
Never leave a link or unlink command in UR with RPT2 on the gateway.
Aether DV can't read this radio's call signs: it asks you to confirm the route. The TH-D75 is reported to send only Fast Data, and Fast Data through repeaters is unverified.

radios.name: TH-D74
radios.summary: Handheld. D-RATS reported to receive only.

steps.title: Using a repeater
items: Set the repeater in the radio's D-STAR settings as for voice (DR or the repeater list).
For this repeater only: UR = CQCQCQ, RPT1 = repeater call and module, RPT2 blank. For the linked reflector: RPT2 = the repeater's gateway (call with G), only with the trustee's agreement.
Never leave a link or unlink command in UR with RPT2 on the gateway.
Reported to receive slow data but not send it, so it can't send through a repeater with slow data. Aether DV asks you to confirm the route if you try.
